questions.q: Why does a CMDB tend to go stale on its own, even if nobody makes a mistake?
options: Infrastructure changes constantly — servers get decommissioned and software gets upgraded — and each change needs a corresponding CI update
ServiceNow automatically deletes CI records after a fixed time period
The cmdb_ci table has a hard limit on how many records it can hold
CIs are read-only once created
questions.explain: A CMDB models infrastructure that is itself always changing, so it has to keep moving just to stay accurate, or it drifts out of date quickly.

questions.q: Why can two legitimate data sources report different values for the same CI field?
options: One of the sources must always be lying or misconfigured
Manual entry, Discovery scans, data imports, and integrations each observe infrastructure differently and at different times, so they can genuinely disagree
ServiceNow only allows one data source per CI, so conflicts never actually happen
Data source conflicts are a myth; real CMDBs never experience this
questions.explain: Different sources look at the world through different mechanisms at different times — the disagreement is genuine, not a sign either source is wrong.

questions.q: What is the quiet effect of a CMDB having no clear ownership for a given class of CI?
options: The CI class is automatically archived
ServiceNow assigns a default owner automatically
Stale or duplicate data sits unchallenged because nobody's job is to notice or fix it
The base cmdb_ci table stops accepting new records of that type
questions.explain: Ownership gaps don't throw errors — they just mean nobody is accountable for catching inaccuracies, so the data quietly drifts.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the honest, most common root cause when a real-world CMDB implementation fails?
options: A technical limitation of the ServiceNow platform itself
Governance and process gaps — unclear ownership, unreconciled sources, nobody noticing staleness
The cmdb_ci table hierarchy being too complex to use
A lack of available CI subclasses for modern infrastructure
questions.explain: Most failed implementations fail on governance, not the platform — which is exactly why Chapter 5 teaches real ownership and stewardship, not just more table structure.

questions.q: Which later chapter in this course directly addresses the data-source-conflict problem introduced in this lesson?
options: Chapter 2's relationship types
Chapter 5's Identification and Reconciliation rules
Chapter 4's Discovery schedules
Chapter 3's CSDM domains
questions.explain: Chapter 5 covers Identification and Reconciliation rules — the real mechanism for resolving which source wins when CI data conflicts.
